# Getting started {#sec-start}

biyos is a C library. A program uses it through one C header, and a Python package calls the same library.

## Installing {#sec-start-install}

The C library comes as `libbiyos.so` on Linux, `libbiyos.dylib` on macOS and `biyos.dll` on Windows. Its folder, the prefix below, holds the header in `include/biyos`, the library in `lib` (the DLL in `bin`) and a CMake package.

The Python package needs Python 3.10 or later and nothing else:

```sh
python -m pip install biyos
```

## The library and its header {#sec-start-layers}

A program includes one header, `biyos/biyos.h`, which needs only `<stddef.h>` and `<stdint.h>`. The library exports the functions of that header and nothing else, so no C++ type or exception reaches the caller.

![The layers of biyos. Each arrow points from a part to one it uses. Only `biyos.h` crosses the library's boundary.](../figures/layers.svg){#fig-layers}

## A first program {#sec-start-program}

This program prints the version of the library, then creates an environment and frees it:

```{.c file="examples/code/c/start.c"}
```

An environment holds the options, the events and the last error of each thread. Every model is made on one. Every call returns `BIYOS_OK` when it succeeds ([Errors](#sec-errors)).

### With CMake

A CMake project finds biyos as a package, of exactly the version it was built as:

```cmake
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.25)
project(app LANGUAGES C)

find_package(biyos 0.1.0 EXACT CONFIG REQUIRED)

add_executable(app app.c)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE biyos::biyos)
```

Configure it with `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<prefix>`. The target `biyos::biyos` brings the include directory.

### Without CMake

On Linux, compile against the header and link the library:

```sh
cc -std=c99 start.c -I <prefix>/include -L <prefix>/lib -lbiyos \
   -Wl,-rpath,<prefix>/lib -o start
./start
```

It prints `biyos 0.1.0`.

## From Python {#sec-start-python}

The package calls the C API through `ctypes`, so every rule of this book holds in Python too. The first program becomes:

```{.python file="examples/code/python/start.py"}
```

The `with` block frees the environment when it ends. [The Python package](#sec-python) covers the rest.
